prompt:
Build a causal two-body axisymmetric point-absorber wave-energy converter. A surface float and a submerged spar/plate must each have rigid-body heave dynamics and physically connected hydrodynamic excitation, radiation, added-mass and hydrostatic-restoring effects. Couple the two bodies through a translational power-take-off (PTO) so that its force acts on their relative heave motion and its absorbed power is calculated from that same force/velocity path. Do not prescribe the body motion, PTO force, or generated power directly.

Read rm3_command from the MATLAB base workspace as a scalar struct with exactly these public fields: wave_height_m, a real scalar from 1.5 to 4.0 m; wave_period_s, a real scalar from 6.5 to 10.0 s; and pto_damping_n_s_m, a real scalar from 600000 to 2000000 N*s/m. Simulate 0 to 80 s.

Log three Timeseries over the full interval with the exact channel names, order, and units below. rm3_body_response has [float_heave_m, float_heave_velocity_m_s, spar_heave_m, spar_heave_velocity_m_s] in [m, m/s, m, m/s]. rm3_pto_response has [relative_heave_m, relative_heave_velocity_m_s, pto_force_n, absorbed_power_w] in [m, m/s, N, W]. rm3_hydrodynamic_response has [wave_elevation_m, float_excitation_force_z_n, float_radiation_force_z_n, float_restoring_force_z_n] in [m, N, N, N]. Every log must begin at 0 s, remain finite, reach 80 s, and have no sample gap greater than 0.1 s.

Save the completed model as cand_XFLUID12.slx in the submission directory.

Submission filename contract: create, edit, and save the final self-contained Simulink model as cand_XFLUID12.slx in the assigned submission directory; keep the latest usable state at that exact path throughout the run.
